And it’s not really about the car accident I was in a few years ago. That was awful, definitely, but this anxiety…it feels bigger than that. It’s about everything and nothing specific at the same time. I worry about gas prices, whether I locked the door, if I sent that email correctly, if my samples at work are going to be contaminated. Even when I'm just trying to read a report, my attention constantly drifts to some new worry, making it impossible to focus on a single sentence. I try to tell myself to stop, but it’s like this invisible force just keeps twisting me up inside."
D011-D018_h024.question_b: It’s been, well, it feels like forever, but probably six or seven months now. After… the incident at work, everything just changed. I can't stop replaying it, even when I try to focus on other things. I used to be so sharp, but now my mind just jumps from that day to other worries, then back again. I try to tell myself to stop, to distract myself, but it’s like my brain has its own agenda. Before, I was good at keeping my work separate, but now every little thing just sets off this constant hum of anxiety. It feels like this worry started right after what happened, and it just hasn’t let up since. I used to love my job, the precision of it all, but now it’s just… overwhelming. I keep thinking something bad is going to happen again.

    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

I try to tell myself to stop, to just focus on what's in front of me, but these worries just keep swirling, no matter what I do. It’s like a broken record in my head that I can’t turn off. It's really affecting my work too; when I'm in the cockpit, my mind drifts. Even though I went through that really rough emergency landing a few years back, this gnawing worry feels different. D011-D018_h025.question_b: Doctor, I’m at my wit's end. After that incident – the emergency landing a few months ago – everything’s just… different. I can’t stop worrying. My co-pilot asked me about a flight plan the other day and I just stared at him, my mind completely blank because I was agonizing over whether I'd checked the fuel correctly on the last trip, even though I knew I had. It’s been constant like this since the landing; I can’t seem to get a handle on it.
